text: Honoré de Balzac's Droll Stories was banned by Canada Customs beginning in 1914, and the book was subject to confiscation as late as 1970. It was also reported banned for obscenity from 1901 to 1923 and again from 1928 to approximately 1973. In New Zealand a Magistrate's Court banned the book in 1935: a bookseller was convicted under the 1910 Act for displaying it, and the magistrate said the work was indecent because its tales glorified immorality and licentiousness and ridiculed purity and virtue.
meta_description: Balzac's Droll Stories was banned by Canada Customs from 1914 and by a New Zealand court in 1935 for indecency.
changes: Place-less 1901-1973 claim flagged as 'also reported'; New Zealand case merged into one sentence.
